newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain parties break with ETA politicians.
newsitem.headline: Spain parties break with ETA politicians.

text.p: Spain's political parties made a united break with Herri Batasuna, the political arm of ETA Basque separatist rebels, on Monday after the group brutally killed a young politician.

"The definitive and total break with Herri Batasuna is now on the record until ETA stops killing or until Herri Batasuna ruptures its alliances in the world of terror," Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja, of the ruling Popular Party, told a news conference after a multi-party anti-terrorism group met.
Herri Batasuna holds two seats in the national congress in addition to its representation in regional parliaments in the northern Basque country and Navarre.
Basque regional party leaders decided on Sunday to cease all cooperation with Herri Batasuna in a statement of condemnation that the Madrid parties ratified "point by point".
Some analysts say the isolation of Herri Batasuna by Basque politicians removes an avenue of peaceful dialogue.
The government in Madrid has a long-standing policy of refusing to talk to ETA, which has killed some 800 people in a nearly 30-year drive for Basque independence, unless it renounces violence.
Mayor Oreja, speaking on the behalf of what he called the democratic political parties, said they would study legislative reforms to better combat terrorism.
He said the huge public outcry against the latest ETA killing would ensure that the initiatives would be lasting.

"The impressive effort that has been made by the millions of Spaniards in all corners of Spain has been a decisive contribution to the fight against terrorism and the effort to bring peace to the Basque region," Mayor Oreja said.
